grades.quote: create, like sys_link, holds two inode locks simultaneously: ip and dp. There is no possibility of deadlock because the inode ip is freshly allocated: no other process in the system will hold ip ’s lock and then try to lock dp.
grades.reason: Provides an inode-locking and deadlock example, but does not explain reference ownership or its separation from locking.

grades.quote: A struct inode pointer returned by iget() is guaranteed to be valid until the corresponding call to iput(); the inode won’t be deleted, and the memory referred to by the pointer won’t be re-used for a different inode. iget() provides non-exclusive access to an inode, so that there can be many pointers to the same inode.
grades.reason: Directly distinguishes reference counts that preserve inode lifetime from sleep-locks that provide exclusive access, explaining how shared references support race prevention without unnecessary locking or deadlock.

grades.quote: A lock provides mutual exclusion, ensuring that only one CPU at a time can hold the lock.
grades.reason: Explains the general purpose of exclusive locking, but not inode reference counts or their separate lifetime-management role.
